title: Variolation in Ming China
summary: Variolation, deliberate inoculation with smallpox material through the nose, was practised in Ming China. A Macao Cultural Institute paper says it first appeared in the Longqing reign (1567-1572), and the CDC's Emerging Infectious Diseases journal records Longqing-era practitioners in Taiping County, Anhui. A Korean review names a 1549 text as the oldest record.

uncertainty.note: Longqing reign dates 1567-1572 are from two sources; a 2026 EID review says practice began no later than the Chenghua-Longqing period (1465-1572); a Korean review dates the oldest text, Douzhen Xinfa, to 1549.

as_recorded.value: no later than the Chenghua–Longqing period of the Ming dynasty (1465–1572 CE)

where.modern_name: Huangshan City, Anhui, China (proxy pin: the Korean review names Huangshan City as the Longqing-era centre; EID names Taiping County, Anhui)

importance.justification: An early documented smallpox inoculation practice; the Macao paper says it reached Europe in the early eighteenth century.
